concepts.def: A push or pull that can change an object's shape, speed or direction. Measured in newtons (N).
The amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms (kg). Does not change with location.
The downward gravitational force on a mass: W = mg, where g ≈ 9.8 N/kg on Earth.
The single force that has the same effect as all forces acting on an object combined.
Contact forces require touching (friction, tension); non-contact act at a distance (gravity, magnetism).
A diagram showing all forces acting on a single object as arrows from its centre.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Motion, Forces & Energy — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Motion, Forces & Energy brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Motion, Forces & Energy.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A 2 kg object accelerates at 4 m/s². What is the resultant force?
What does it mean if the resultant force on an object is zero?
options: The object is either stationary or moving at constant velocity.

numericals.q: Calculate the weight in newtons of a 5 kg mass on Earth (g = 9.8 N/kg).

free_texts.q: What is the SI unit of force?
